title.en: Volume 237 Biographies 125: Fu Haoli, Jiang Zhili, Bao Jianjie, Tian Dayi, Feng Yingjing, Wu Zongyao, Wu Baoxiu, Hua Yu

sentences.zh: 傅好禮姜誌禮包見捷田大益馮應京

translations.literal: Fu Haoli, Jiang Zhili, Bao Jianjie, Tian Dayi, Feng Yingjing
translations.idiomatic: Fu Haoli, Jiang Zhili, Bao Jianjie, Tian Dayi, and Feng Yingjing

sentences.zh: （何棟如王之翰卞孔時）〉

translations.literal: (He Dongru, Wang Zhihan, Bian Kongshi)〉
translations.idiomatic: (He Dongru, Wang Zhihan, and Bian Kongshi)]〉

sentences.zh: 吳宗堯吳寶秀華鈺

translations.literal: Wu Zongyao, Wu Baoxiu, Hua Yu
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zongyao, Wu Baoxiu, and Hua Yu

sentences.zh: （王正誌）〉

translations.literal: (Wang Zhengzhi)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Wang Zhengzhi)]〉

sentences.zh: 傅好禮，字伯恭，固安人。

translations.literal: Fu Haoli, courtesy name Bogong, was a man of Gu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Haoli, whose courtesy name was Bogong, came from Gu'an.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the second year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 知涇縣，治最，入為御史。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Jing County; his governance was rated supreme, and he entered office as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Jing County he earned the highest rating for his administration, then was appointed a censor.

sentences.zh: 嘗陳時政，請節遊宴，停內操，罷外戚世封，止山陵行幸，又上崇實、杜漸諸疏。

translations.literal: He once presented the affairs of the time, requesting moderation in banquets and excursions, cessation of inner-palace drill, abolition of hereditary enfeoffment for maternal kin, and an end to imperial visits to mountain tombs; he also submitted several memorials such as "Honoring Substance" and "Blocking Gradual Harm."
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly addressed current policy, urging the emperor to cut back on feasting and travel, halt palace drill troops, end perpetual enfeoffment of consort kin, and stop touring imperial tombs, and he also submitted memorials on honoring substance over show and on checking gradual abuses.

sentences.zh: 語皆剴直。

translations.literal: His words were all incisive and direct.
translations.idiomatic: Every statement was sharp and forthright.

sentences.zh: 巡按浙江。

translations.literal: He toured and inspected Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as touring censor for Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 歲大侵，條上荒政。

translations.literal: That year suffered great famine; he itemized and submitted policies for famine relief.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck severely that year, he laid out a full program of relief measures.

sentences.zh: 行部湖州，用便宜發漕折銀萬兩，易粟振饑民。

translations.literal: When his tour reached Huzhou, he used discretionary authority to release ten thousand taels of transport-grain silver conversion funds, exchanged it for grain, and relieved the starving people.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Huzhou in the course of his tour, he used emergency powers to release ten thousand taels earmarked from grain-transport conversion funds, bought grain with it, and fed the starving.

sentences.zh: 改按山東。

translations.literal: He was transferred to tour and inspect Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as touring censor for Shandong.

sentences.zh: 泰安州同知張壽朋當貶秩，文選郎謝廷寀用為永平推官，謂州同知六品，而推官七品也。

translations.literal: Zhang Shoupeng, assistant prefect of Tai'an Prefecture, ought to have been demoted in rank; the Bureau of Appointments clerk Xie Tingcai appointed him investigating censor of Yongping, saying that a prefectural assistant was sixth rank while an investigating censor was seventh.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shoupeng, the Tai'an assistant prefect, should have been demoted, but Xie Tingcai of the Bureau of Appointments posted him as Yongping investigating censor on the pretext that a sixth-rank assistant prefect could be shifted to a seventh-rank investigating post.

sentences.zh: 好禮馳疏劾其非制，廷寀坐停俸，壽朋改調。

translations.literal: Haoli sent a hurried memorial impeaching this as contrary to regulation; Tingcai was punished with suspension of salary, and Shoupeng was transferred elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Haoli rushed in a memorial charging irregular appointment; Tingcai had his salary suspended, and Shoupeng was reassigned.

sentences.zh: 好禮尋謝病歸。

translations.literal: Before long Haoli resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Haoli soon retired citing illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 召進光祿少卿，改太常。

translations.literal: He was summoned and advanced to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then transferred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled, made Vice Minister of Imperial Entertainments, and then transferred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 時稅使四出，海內騷然。

translations.literal: At the time tax commissioners went out in all directions, and the realm was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Tax agents were being dispatched everywhere, throwing the empire into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 二十六年冬，奸民張禮等偽為官吏，群小百十人分據近京要地，稅民間雜物，弗予，捶至死。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twenty-sixth year, scoundrels such as Zhang Li impersonated officials; a band of more than a hundred petty men seized key sites near the capital, levied taxes on miscellaneous goods in the populace, and when payment was refused beat people to death.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in year twenty-six, ruffians led by Zhang Li posed as officials; gangs of well over a hundred men seized strategic points around the capital, taxed everyday goods, and beat anyone who would not pay until he was dead.

sentences.zh: 好禮極論其害，因言：「自朝鮮用兵，畿民富者貧，貧者死，思亂已久，奈何又虐征。

translations.literal: Haoli argued to the utmost about the harm, then said: "Since the war in Korea, the people of the capital region—those who were rich have become poor, those who were poor have died; thoughts of rebellion have long existed—how can we again impose cruel levies.
translations.idiomatic: Haoli laid out the damage at length and added: "Since the Korean campaign, the rich around the capital have been ruined and the poor have died; unrest has been brewing for years—why heap on more crushing taxes.

sentences.zh: 國家縱貧，亦不當頭會箕斂，括細民續命之脂膏；

translations.literal: Even if the state were poor, it still ought not to levy head-by-head and rake together, squeezing from common people the fat that sustains their lives;
translations.idiomatic: Even a state in want should not wring every household dry and scrape away the last resources by which ordinary people stay alive;

sentences.zh: 況奸徒所得千萬，輸朝廷者什一耳，陛下何利為之。」

translations.literal: Moreover, what the villains gain runs to millions, while what reaches the court is only one part in ten—what profit is there for Your Majesty in this.
translations.idiomatic: And when villains pocket millions while the court receives perhaps a tenth, what gain could Your Majesty possibly see in it.

sentences.zh: 奏入，四日未報，復具疏請。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, four days passed with no reply; he again prepared a memorial requesting action.
translations.idiomatic: After the memorial was submitted, four days passed without response, so he filed another urging the throne to act.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，傳旨鐫三級，出之外。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and transmitted an order that he be demoted three ranks and sent outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and ordered him demoted three ranks and expelled from the capital.

sentences.zh: 大理卿吳定疏救。

translations.literal: The Minister of Punishments Wu Ding submitted a memorial in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ding, Minister of Punishments, memorialized in his defense.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，謫好禮大同廣昌典史，定鐫三級，調邊方。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still angrier, demoting Haoli to clerk of Guangchang in Datong, demoting Ding three ranks, and transferring him to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor only grew angrier: Haoli was banished to the post of Guangchang clerk in Datong, Ding was cut three ranks and sent to the borderlands.

sentences.zh: 言官復交章論救，斥定為民。

translations.literal: Censors again submitted memorials one after another pleading for mercy; Ding was dismissed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Censors again flooded the court with pleas for leniency, and Ding was stripped of office and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 既而帝思好禮言，下其疏，命廠衛嚴緝，逮禮等二十八人詔獄，其害乃除。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor reflected on Haoli's words, issued his memorial, ordered the palace agents to arrest strictly, seized Li and twenty-eight others into the imperial prison, and the harm was then removed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor took Haoli's warning to heart, circulated his memorial, ordered the secret police to hunt the culprits down, and had Li and twenty-eight others thrown into the imperial prison—only then was the abuse ended.

sentences.zh: 好禮之官，未幾，請急歸。

translations.literal: Haoli in office, before long requested urgent leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Haoli had not long been back in office when he asked leave on urgent family grounds.

sentences.zh: 家居十五年卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home fifteen years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for fifteen years and then died.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，贈太常卿。

translations.literal: During the Tianqi reign he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tianqi emperor he was posthumously made Grand Master of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 姜誌禮，字立之，丹陽人。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhili, courtesy name Lizhi, was a man of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhili, whose courtesy name was Lizhi, came from Danyang.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十七年進士。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi degree in the seventeenth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 歷建昌、衢州推官，入為大理評事。

translations.literal: He successively served as investigating censor of Jianchang and Quzhou, then entered office as reviewer in the Court of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He served as investigating censor in Jianchang and Quzhou in turn, then entered the Court of Punishments as a reviewing official.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，以囚多瘐死，疏言：「犴狴之間，一日斃十五人。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, because many prisoners died of illness in confinement, he memorialized: "Between the prison walls, fifteen persons die in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-three, seeing prisoners dying in droves from neglect, he wrote: "Inside the jails, fifteen people die in a single day.

sentences.zh: 積日而計，亦何紀極！

translations.literal: Calculated day by day, how can one reckon the limit!
translations.idiomatic: Day after day, who can count the toll!

sentences.zh: 又況海內小民，罹災寢而轉死溝壑，及為礦稅所羅織、貂珰所攫噬、含冤畢命者，又復何限！

translations.literal: Moreover, how limitless are the common people within the seas who, stricken by disaster, waste away and turn to die in ditches and gullies, and those who, ensnared by mining taxes, seized and devoured by sable-capped eunuchs, end their lives bearing injustice!
translations.idiomatic: And beyond the prisons, how many common folk across the realm waste away in famine and die in ditches, or are ruined by mining levies, torn apart by eunuch agents, and perish with grievances never heard—who can number them!

sentences.zh: 乞亟為矜宥，勿久淹系，且盡除礦稅，毋使宵人竊弄魁柄，賊虐丞黎。」

translations.literal: I beg that mercy be shown swiftly, that long detention not continue, and that mining taxes be wholly abolished, lest night-roaming men secretly wield the chief handle and rob and abuse the people.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to show mercy at once, release those held too long, and abolish mining taxes altogether, lest villains seize real power and prey on the people.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The throne did not respond.

sentences.zh: 歷刑部員外，出為泉州知府，遷廣東副使，並有聲。

translations.literal: He successively served as a vice director in the Ministry of Punishments, went out as prefect of Quanzhou, and was promoted to Vice Commissioner of Guangdong—all with reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the Ministry of Punishments, became prefect of Quanzhou, and was promoted to Guangdong vice commissioner, earning a strong reputation at each post.

sentences.zh: 進山東右參政，分守登、萊。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Right Vice Commissioner of Shandong, with divided defense of Deng and Lai.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Commissioner of Shandong with responsibility for the Dengzhou and Laizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 福王封國河南，詔賜田二百萬畝，跨山東、湖廣境。

translations.literal: The Prince of Fu was enfeoffed in Henan; an edict granted him two million mu of fields, straddling the borders of Shandong and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu was enfeoffed in Henan, an edict granted him two million mu of land spanning Shandong and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 既之國，遣中貴徐進督山東賦，勢甚張。

translations.literal: After he had gone to his state, he dispatched the eunuch Xu Jin to supervise Shandong levies, and his power was very overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Once the prince had taken up residence, he sent the eunuch Xu Jin to oversee Shandong taxes, and Xu wielded enormous power.

sentences.zh: 誌禮抗疏曰：「臣所轄二郡，民不聊生，且與倭鄰，不宜有藩府莊田以擾茲土也明甚。

translations.literal: Zhili submitted a defiant memorial saying: "The two prefectures under my jurisdiction—the people cannot sustain life, and moreover we border the Japanese; that there should not be princely estate fields to disturb this land is abundantly clear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili protested in a bold memorial: "In the two prefectures I govern the people can barely survive, and we lie next to the Japanese coast—it should be obvious that princely estates must not be imposed on this ground.

sentences.zh: 且自高皇帝迄今累十餘世，封王子弟多矣，有賜田二萬頃，延連數十郡者乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, from the August Founder to the present there have been more than ten generations; many princes and imperial sons have been enfeoffed—has there ever been a grant of twenty thousand qing of fields extending across dozens of prefectures?
translations.idiomatic: Since the Hongwu founder, more than ten generations have passed and countless princes have been enfeoffed—when has any ever received twenty thousand qing stretching across dozens of commanderies?

sentences.zh: 繼此而封，尚有瑞、惠、桂三王也。

translations.literal: Following this enfeoffment, there are still the three princes of Rui, Hui, and Gui.
translations.idiomatic: After this grant there remain the Princes of Rui, Hui, and Gui still to be provided for.

sentences.zh: 倘比例以請，將予之乎，不予之乎？

translations.literal: If they request by proportional precedent, will you grant or not grant?
translations.idiomatic: If they ask on the same scale, will Your Majesty grant or refuse?

sentences.zh: 況國祚靈長，久且未艾。

translations.literal: Moreover, the dynastic fortune is numinous and long; far from ending, it has not yet peaked.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the dynasty's fortune is enduring and shows no sign of fading.

sentences.zh: 嗣是天家子姓，各援今日故事以請，臣恐方內土田，不足共諸藩分裂也。」

translations.literal: Thereafter the sons and surnames of the celestial house will each cite today's precedent to request; I fear the land within the realm will not suffice for all the princedoms to divide among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Every imperial clansman to come will cite today's precedent; I fear there will not be enough land in the empire to parcel out among all the princes.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，貶三秩為廣西僉事。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and demoted him three ranks to Commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and demoted him three ranks to Guangxi commissioner.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷江西參議。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Jiangxi as participating administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he was moved to Jiangxi as a participating administrator.

sentences.zh: 天啟三年，由浙江副使入為尚寶少卿，尋進卿。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianqi, from Zhejiang Vice Commissioner he entered as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Seals, and soon was advanced to Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianqi he came in from Zhejiang as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Seals and was soon promoted to Director.

sentences.zh: 河南進玉璽，魏忠賢欲誌禮疏獻之。

translations.literal: Henan presented a jade seal; Wei Zhongxian wanted Zhili to memorialize presenting it.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan presented a jade seal, Wei Zhongxian wanted Zhili to memorialize its presentation to the throne.

sentences.zh: 誌禮不可。

translations.literal: Zhili would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili refused.

sentences.zh: 忠賢怒，令私人劾其衰老，遂乞休。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was angry, had his private associates impeach him for senility, and he then requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was enraged, had his men accuse Zhili of senility, and Zhili then asked to retire from office.

sentences.zh: 詔加太常少卿致仕，已而削奪。

translations.literal: An edict added Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices for his retirement, but soon his honors were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices in retirement, but soon those honors were revoked.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，復官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chongzhen reign his titles were restored.

sentences.zh: 誌禮性淳樸，所居多政績，亦以行誼稱於鄉。

translations.literal: Zhili's nature was simple and honest; wherever he served he mostly had administrative achievements, and he was also praised in his home district for conduct and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili was plain and upright by nature, left a record of solid achievement wherever he served, and was respected at home for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 包見捷，雲南臨安衛人。

translations.literal: Bao Jianjie was a man of Lin'an Guard in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Jianjie came from Lin'an Guard in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十七年進士。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the seventeenth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授戶科給事中，屢遷都給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Bachelor, appointed supervising secretary of the Household Section, and repeatedly promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, was made supervising secretary of the Household Section, and rose repeatedly to Chief Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 奸人李本立請采珠廣東，帝命中官李敬偕往。

translations.literal: The scoundrel Li Benli requested pearl-diving in Guangdong; the emperor ordered the eunuch Li Jing to go together with him.
translations.idiomatic: When the schemer Li Benli proposed pearl-fishing in Guangdong, the emperor sent the eunuch Li Jing along with him.

sentences.zh: 見捷極言其害，不聽。

translations.literal: Jianjie argued to the utmost about the harm; he was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Jianjie protested at length about the harm, but was ignored.

sentences.zh: 時小人蜂起言利。

translations.literal: At the time petty men swarmed forth speaking of profit.
translations.idiomatic: Petty profiteers were swarming forward with schemes.

sentences.zh: 千戶李仁請稅湖口商舟，命中官李道往。

translations.literal: The battalion commander Li Ren requested taxing merchant boats at Hukou; the emperor ordered the eunuch Li Dao to go.
translations.idiomatic: Battalion commander Li Ren proposed taxing merchant vessels at Hukou, and the emperor dispatched the eunuch Li Dao.

sentences.zh: 主簿田應璧請賣兩淮沒官余鹽，令稅使魯保兼理。

translations.literal: The registrar Tian Yingbi requested selling surplus confiscated salt of the two Huai circuits, ordering the tax commissioner Lu Bao to administer it jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Registrar Tian Yingbi urged selling surplus confiscated salt from the two Huai regions and putting tax agent Lu Bao in charge.

sentences.zh: 見捷等並力爭。

translations.literal: Jianjie and others together strove in opposition.
translations.idiomatic: Jianjie and his colleagues fought the measures together.

sentences.zh: 頃之，令道、保節制有司。

translations.literal: Before long, Dao and Bao were ordered to control and direct the regular officials.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Dao and Bao were empowered to command the regular civil officials.

sentences.zh: 見捷又陳不便者數事。

translations.literal: Jianjie again presented several matters of inconvenience.
translations.idiomatic: Jianjie again listed several harmful consequences.

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: None received reply.
translations.idiomatic: None of his memorials received a response.

sentences.zh: 益都知縣吳宗堯劾稅使陳增不法，見捷因請盡罷礦稅。

translations.literal: The Yidu magistrate Wu Zongyao impeached the tax commissioner Chen Zeng for unlawful conduct; Jianjie thereupon requested complete abolition of mining taxes.
translations.idiomatic: When Yidu magistrate Wu Zongyao impeached tax agent Chen Zeng for abuses, Jianjie seized the moment to demand an end to all mining levies.

sentences.zh: 無已，先撤增還。

translations.literal: There was no end to it; first Zeng was withdrawn and recalled.
translations.idiomatic: The court would not go that far, but Chen Zeng was recalled first.

sentences.zh: 未幾，天津稅使王朝死，見捷請勿遣代。

translations.literal: Before long the Tianjin tax commissioner Wang Chao died; Jianjie requested that no replacement be sent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Tianjin tax agent Wang Chao died, and Jianjie asked that no successor be sent.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，切責。

translations.literal: He offended the imperial will and was sharply rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: He offended the throne and was sharply rebuked.

sentences.zh: 以馬堂代朝。

translations.literal: Ma Tang was used to replace Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Tang was appointed in Wang Chao's place.

sentences.zh: 見捷又劾堂、保及浙江劉忠。

translations.literal: Jianjie again impeached Tang, Bao, and Liu Zhong of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jianjie then impeached Tang, Bao, and Liu Zhong in Zhejiang as well.

sentences.zh: 帝不納，益遣高寀、暨祿、李鳳榷稅於京口、儀真、廣東，並專敕行事。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept it, and further dispatched Gao Cai, Ji Lu, and Li Feng to monopolize taxes at Jingkou, Yizhen, and Guangdong, all with special edicts to act.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected him and instead sent Gao Cai, Ji Lu, and Li Feng to levy taxes at Jingkou, Yizhen, and Guangdong, each with a special edict granting full authority.

sentences.zh: 又以奸人閻大經言，命高淮征稅遼東。

translations.literal: Again following the words of the scoundrel Yan Dajing, he ordered Gao Huai to levy taxes in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: On the advice of the schemer Yan Dajing he also ordered Gao Huai to tax Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 見捷等累請停罷，至是言：「遼左神京肩臂，視他鎮尤重。

translations.literal: Jianjie and others repeatedly requested cessation; at this point they said: "Liaodong to the left is shoulder and arm to the divine capital, more important than other garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Jianjie and others had repeatedly demanded a halt; now they wrote: "Liaodong is the shoulder guarding the capital and matters more than any other frontier.

sentences.zh: 奸徒敢為禍首，陛下不懲以三尺，急罷開采，則遼事必不可為，而國步且隨之矣。」

translations.literal: Villains dare to be calamity's head; if Your Majesty does not punish them with the three-foot law and urgently halt mining levies, then Liaodong affairs certainly cannot be accomplished, and the nation's pace will follow in ruin.
translations.idiomatic: If villains are allowed to start this trouble and Your Majesty does not punish them under the law and stop the mining levies at once, Liaodong cannot be held and the dynasty itself will stagger.

sentences.zh: 遼東撫按及山海主事吳鐘英相繼爭。

translations.literal: The Liaodong grand coordinator and regional inspector, and the Shanhai Registrar Wu Zhongying, successively contended as well.
translations.idiomatic: The Liaodong governor-general and censor, and Shanhai registrar Wu Zhongying, protested in turn.

sentences.zh: 皆不納。

translations.literal: None was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: None of these pleas was heeded.

sentences.zh: 時中外爭礦稅者無慮百十疏，見捷言尤數，帝心銜之。

translations.literal: At the time those within and without the court contending over mining taxes were no fewer than a hundred-odd memorials; Jianjie's words were especially numerous, and the emperor bore resentment in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: By then well over a hundred memorials from inside and outside court were fighting mining taxes; Jianjie had spoken more often than anyone, and the emperor bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 居數日，又率司官極論，乃謫見捷貴州布政司都事，余停俸一年。

translations.literal: Within several days, he again led the bureau officials in extreme argument; then Jianjie was demoted to Chief Clerk of the Guizhou Provincial Administration Commission, and the rest had salary suspended one year.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he led his entire bureau in another fierce protest; Jianjie was banished to chief clerk in the Guizhou provincial administration, and the others had their salaries suspended for a year.

sentences.zh: 大學士沈一貫、給事中趙完璧等先後論救，完璧等亦坐停俸。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan, the supervising secretary Zhao Wanbi, and others successively memorialized in defense; Wanbi and others also were punished with salary suspension.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan, supervising secretary Zhao Wanbi, and others pleaded for mercy in turn; Wanbi and his allies lost a year's salary as well.

sentences.zh: 見捷尋引疾去。

translations.literal: Before long Jianjie cited illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: Jianjie soon retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，起興業知縣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was raised as magistrate of Xingye.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-four he was recalled as magistrate of Xingye.

sentences.zh: 累遷太僕少卿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 久之，以右僉都御史巡撫江西。

translations.literal: After a long time, as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief he toured and pacified Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，召拜吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended, he was summoned and appointed Right Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong took the throne, he was summoned as Right Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 明年卒官。

translations.literal: The next year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office the following year.

sentences.zh: 田大益，字博真，四川定遠人。

translations.literal: Tian Dayi, courtesy name Bozhen, was a man of Dingyuan in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dayi, whose courtesy name was Bozhen, came from Dingyuan in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi degree in the fourteenth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 授鐘祥知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Zhongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Zhongxiang.

sentences.zh: 擢兵科給事中，疏論日本封貢可虞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising secretary of the Military Section and memorialized that Japan's enfeoffment and tribute were cause for concern.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to supervising secretary of the Military Section, he warned that Japan's request for investiture and tribute was dangerous.

sentences.zh: 又言：「東征之役，在將士，則當據今日之斬馘以論功；

translations.literal: He also said: "In the eastern campaign, as for officers and soldiers, one should judge merit according to today's decapitations and captures;
translations.idiomatic: He also argued: "In the eastern campaign, for the rank and file rewards should follow today's counts of enemy killed;

sentences.zh: 在主帥，則當視後日之成敗以定議。」

translations.literal: as for the commander-in-chief, one should view later days' success or failure to fix judgment.
translations.idiomatic: for the supreme commander, judgment should wait on whether the campaign ultimately succeeds or fails.

sentences.zh: 時韙其言。

translations.literal: At the time his words were approved as correct.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court praised his advice.

sentences.zh: 母喪除，起補戶科。

translations.literal: When mourning for his mother ended, he was raised to fill a vacancy in the Household Section.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period ended, he was recalled to fill a vacancy in the Household Section.

sentences.zh: 二十八年十月，疏言：「陛下受命日久，驕泰乘之，布列豺狼，殄滅善類，民無所措，靡不蓄怨含憤，覬一旦有事。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twenty-eighth year he memorialized: "Your Majesty has received the Mandate for a long time; arrogance and excess have taken hold, jackals and wolves are arrayed, good men are destroyed, the people have nowhere to turn, and none fail to harbor resentment and rage, watching for a sudden crisis.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year twenty-eight he wrote: "Your Majesty has held the throne long enough for arrogance to take root; wolves are posted everywhere, good men are destroyed, and the people have nowhere to turn—all hoarding resentment and waiting for trouble to break.

sentences.zh: 願陛下惕然警覺，敬天地，嚴祖宗，毋輕臣工，毋戕民命，毋任閹人，毋縱群小，毋務暴刻，毋甘怠荒，急改敗轍，遵治規，用保祖宗無疆之業。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would be alert and vigilant with fear, revere Heaven and Earth, honor the ancestors, not slight the officials, not harm the people's lives, not employ eunuchs, not indulge petty men, not pursue cruelty and harshness, not willingly sink into idleness and neglect, urgently change the failing course, follow the norms of governance, and thereby preserve the ancestors' boundless enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to wake in alarm: revere Heaven and Earth, honor your ancestors, do not slight your ministers, do not waste the people's lives, do not trust eunuchs, do not indulge petty men, do not pursue cruelty, do not sink into sloth, change course at once, follow the rules of good government, and preserve the boundless inheritance of your house.

sentences.zh: 未幾，極陳礦稅六害，言：

translations.literal: Before long he argued to the utmost about the six harms of mining taxes, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he laid out at length the six evils of mining levies, writing:

sentences.zh: 內臣務為劫奪，以應上求。

translations.literal: Inner eunuchs strove to plunder and seize, to meet the ruler's demands.
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs strove to plunder and extort to satisfy the throne's demands.

sentences.zh: 礦不必穴，而稅不必商；

translations.literal: mines need not be in shafts, and taxes need not be on merchants;
translations.idiomatic: Mines need not be dug in hillsides, and taxes need not fall on merchants alone;

sentences.zh: 民間丘隴阡陌，皆礦也，官吏農工，皆入稅之人也。

translations.literal: every mound and field path among the people became a mine, and officials, farmers, and artisans all became persons subject to tax.
translations.idiomatic: every village mound and field path was declared a mine, and officials, farmers, and artisans alike were taxed.

sentences.zh: 公私騷然，脂膏殫竭。

translations.literal: public and private were in uproar, and the people's fat was utterly drained.
translations.idiomatic: Public and private life were thrown into chaos until the people's substance was utterly drained.

sentences.zh: 向所謂軍國正供，反致缺損。

translations.literal: What had been called the regular supply for army and state instead suffered shortage.
translations.idiomatic: The regular revenues for army and state actually fell short.

sentences.zh: 即令有司威以刀鋸，只足驅民而速之亂耳。

translations.literal: Even if the officials threatened with blade and saw, it would only suffice to drive the people and hasten rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Even if officials threatened the people with blade and saw, they would only drive them faster toward revolt.

sentences.zh: 此所謂斂巧必蹶也。

translations.literal: This is what is called: clever exaction must end in collapse.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first evil: clever exaction must end in collapse.

sentences.zh: 陛下嘗以礦稅之役為裕國愛民。

translations.literal: Your Majesty once regarded the mining-tax undertaking as enriching the state and loving the people.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty once claimed that mining levies would enrich the state and benefit the people.

sentences.zh: 然內庫日進不已，未嘗少佐軍國之需。

translations.literal: Yet the inner treasury daily received without cease and never once aided army and state needs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the inner treasury swelled day by day without ever easing the needs of army or state.

sentences.zh: 四海之人，方反唇切齒，而冀以計智甘言，掩天下耳目，其可得乎！

translations.literal: The people within the four seas were just turning lips and grinding teeth, yet one hoped with schemes and sweet words to cover the world's eyes and ears—how could that be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven were gnashing their teeth in rage—how could sweet words and clever schemes possibly deceive the world!

sentences.zh: 此所謂名偽必敗也。

translations.literal: This is what is called: false name must end in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second evil: a false name must end in defeat.

sentences.zh: 財積而不用，祟將隨之。

translations.literal: Wealth piled up yet unused—calamity will follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth hoarded but unused draws calamity in its wake.

sentences.zh: 脫巾不已，至於揭竿，適為奸雄睥睨之資。

translations.literal: Casting off headcloths without end, reaching the point of raising poles—this just becomes capital for villainous heroes to look down upon.
translations.idiomatic: Unrest spreads from banditry to open rebellion, furnishing ambitious traitors with their opportunity.

sentences.zh: 此時雖家給人予，亦且蹴之覆之而不可及矣。

translations.literal: At that time, even if every household had its provision, one would still kick it over and overturn it and not reach it.
translations.idiomatic: By then, even if every household were stocked with grain, the state could not recover what had been kicked over and ruined.

sentences.zh: 此所謂賄聚必散也。

translations.literal: This is what is called: bribes gathered must scatter.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third evil: hoarded wealth must scatter.

sentences.zh: 夫眾心不可傷也。

translations.literal: The hearts of the multitude must not be wounded.
translations.idiomatic: The people's hearts must not be wounded.

sentences.zh: 今天下上自簪纓，下至耕夫販婦，茹苦含辛、搤諲側目、而無所控訴者，蓋已久矣。

translations.literal: Today under Heaven, from the girdled caps above to the plowman and peddling woman below, those who swallow bitterness and hold back sighs, clench fists and cast sidelong glances yet have nowhere to appeal—this has long been so.
translations.idiomatic: Today, from officials in their caps down to farmers and market women, countless people swallow bitterness, clench their fists, and glare in helpless rage with nowhere to appeal—this has gone on far too long.

sentences.zh: 一旦土崩勢成，家為仇，人為敵，眾心齊倡，而海內因以大潰。

translations.literal: Once the earth-splitting momentum forms, families become foes and persons become enemies; the multitude's hearts sing together, and within the seas the realm thereby collapses greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Once the ground gives way, every household becomes an enemy and every person a foe; when all hearts rise together, the empire collapses at once.

sentences.zh: 此所謂怨極必亂也。

translations.literal: This is what is called: resentment at the extreme must bring chaos.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth evil: resentment pushed to the limit must bring chaos.

sentences.zh: 國家全盛二百三十餘年，已屬陽九，而東征西討以求快意。

translations.literal: The state in full vigor for more than two hundred thirty years has already entered the yang-nine decline, yet campaigns east and west are waged to seek momentary satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty has flourished for more than two hundred thirty years and already stands in its late yang-nine phase, yet campaigns east and west are waged merely to gratify whim.

sentences.zh: 上之蕩主心，下之耗國脈。

translations.literal: Above it unsettles the ruler's heart; below it drains the nation's pulse.
translations.idiomatic: Above, it unsettles the ruler's mind; below, it drains the nation's lifeblood.

sentences.zh: 二豎固而良醫走，死氣索而大命傾。

translations.literal: The two petty men hold firm while good physicians flee; the breath of death is drawn tight while the great mandate tilts.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men hold power while good physicians flee; the breath of death tightens while the dynasty's mandate tilts toward ruin.

sentences.zh: 此所謂禍遲必大也。

translations.literal: This is what is called: disaster delayed must be great.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth evil: disaster delayed grows great.

sentences.zh: 陛下矜奮自賢，沈迷不返。

translations.literal: Your Majesty prides himself on vigor and deems himself worthy, sunk in delusion without return.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty prides himself on vigor and deems himself wise, yet sinks deeper without turning back.

sentences.zh: 以豪珰奸弁為腹心，以金錢珠玉為命脈。

translations.literal: He takes overbearing eunuchs and treacherous military officers as his heart and belly, and gold, cash, pearls, and jade as his life-pulse.
translations.idiomatic: He takes overbearing eunuchs and treacherous officers as his inner circle, and gold, cash, pearls, and jade as his lifeblood.

sentences.zh: 藥石之言，褎如充耳。

translations.literal: Words like medicine and stone fill the sleeves as if plugging the ears.
translations.idiomatic: Remedial counsel fills his sleeves yet never reaches his ears.

sentences.zh: 即令逢、幹剖心，臯夔進諫，亦安能解其惑哉！

translations.literal: Even if Peng and Gan laid open their hearts and Gao Yao and Kui advanced remonstrance, how could they resolve his delusion!
translations.idiomatic: Even if Peng and Gan laid open their hearts and Gao Yao and Kui remonstrated in person, how could they break through such delusion!

sentences.zh: 此所謂意迷難救也。

translations.literal: This is what is called: mind deluded, hard to save.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sixth evil: a deluded mind is hard to save.

sentences.zh: 此六者，今之大患。

translations.literal: These six are today's great calamities.
translations.idiomatic: These six are the great calamities of our age.

sentences.zh: 臣畏死不言，則負陛下，陛下拒諫不納，則危宗社。

translations.literal: If your servant fears death and does not speak, he fails Your Majesty; if Your Majesty rejects remonstrance and does not accept it, the ancestral altars are endangered.
translations.idiomatic: If I fear death and stay silent, I fail Your Majesty; if Your Majesty rejects counsel, the altars of state are endangered.

sentences.zh: 願深察而力反之。

translations.literal: I wish deep scrutiny and strenuous reversal.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to examine these evils deeply and reverse course with all your strength.

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: None received reply.
translations.idiomatic: None of his memorials received a response.

sentences.zh: 明年，疏論湖廣稅監陳奉，救僉事馮應京。

translations.literal: The next year he memorialized on the Huguang tax commissioner Chen Feng and pleaded to save Vice Commissioner Feng Yingjing.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he memorialized against the Huguang tax agent Chen Feng and pleaded for Vice Commissioner Feng Yingjing.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，切責。

translations.literal: He offended the imperial will and was sharply rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: He offended the throne and was sharply rebuked.

sentences.zh: 時武昌民以應京被逮，群聚鼓噪，欲殺奉，奉逃匿楚府以免。

translations.literal: At the time the people of Wuchang, because Yingjing had been seized, gathered in crowds beating drums and clamoring, intending to kill Feng; Feng fled and hid in the Chu princely residence to escape.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Wuchang learned that Yingjing had been arrested, they gathered in uproar intending to kill Feng; Feng fled and hid in the Prince of Chu's residence to escape.

sentences.zh: 大益因上言：「陛下驅率狼虎，飛而食人，使天下之人，剝膚而吸髓，重足而累息，以致天災地坼，山崩川竭。

translations.literal: Dayi thereupon submitted: "Your Majesty drives wolves and tigers, making them fly forth to devour people, causing all under Heaven to have skin stripped and marrow sucked, to stand on tiptoe with layered breaths, until Heaven's disasters and earth's splits, mountains collapsing and rivers drying up.
translations.idiomatic: Dayi then wrote: "Your Majesty drives wolves and tigers to fly forth and devour the people, stripping skin and sucking marrow until all under Heaven tread on tiptoe and hold their breath, bringing on Heaven's disasters, earth's splits, mountains collapsing, and rivers running dry.

sentences.zh: 釁自上開，憤由怨積，奈何欲塗民耳目，以自解釋，謾曰權宜哉！

translations.literal: The quarrel opened from above, rage accumulated from resentment—how can one wish to smear the people's eyes and ears to explain oneself away, falsely calling it expedient!
translations.idiomatic: The trouble began at court and rage built from long resentment—how can Your Majesty smear the people's eyes and ears with talk of 'expediency' to excuse yourself!

sentences.zh: 今楚人以奉故，沈使者不返矣，且欲甘心巡撫大臣矣。

translations.literal: Now because of Feng the people of Chu have sunk the envoy and he does not return, and they even wish to vent their hearts' satisfaction on the grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Now, because of Feng, the people of Chu have drowned an envoy who will never return, and they even seek the life of the grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 中朝使臣不敢入境偵緩急，逾兩月矣。

translations.literal: Central-court envoys dare not enter the territory to scout urgency and ease; it has exceeded two months.
translations.idiomatic: Central envoys have not dared enter the province to assess the crisis for more than two months.

sentences.zh: 四方觀聽，惟在楚人。

translations.literal: The four directions watch and listen—only upon the people of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: All the realm is watching what the people of Chu will do next.

sentences.zh: 臣意陛下必且曠然易慮，立罷礦稅，以靖四方，奈何猶戀戀不能自割也！

translations.literal: Your servant thinks Your Majesty must surely broadly change his mind and immediately abolish mining taxes to pacify the four directions—how can he still cling and be unable to cut himself off!
translations.idiomatic: I believed Your Majesty would surely change course at once and abolish mining levies to pacify the realm—why do you still cling to them and refuse to let go!

sentences.zh: 夫天下至貴，而金玉珠寶至賤也。

translations.literal: Under Heaven is supremely precious, while gold, jade, pearls, and gems are supremely base.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is supremely precious; gold, jade, pearls, and gems are supremely base.

sentences.zh: 積金玉珠寶若泰山，不可市天下尺寸地；

translations.literal: Pile gold, jade, pearls, and gems like Mount Tai—you cannot purchase a foot of land under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Pile gold and gems high as Mount Tai and you still cannot buy a foot of the realm;

sentences.zh: 而失天下，又何用金玉珠寶為哉！

translations.literal: yet if you lose under Heaven, what use are gold, jade, pearls, and gems!
translations.idiomatic: and if you lose the realm, what use are gold and gems!

sentences.zh: 今四方萬姓，見陛下遇楚事而無變誌，知禍必不解，必且群起為變。

translations.literal: Now the myriad clans of the four directions, seeing Your Majesty meet the Chu affair without change of resolve, know calamity certainly will not dissolve and will surely rise together in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Now the people everywhere see Your Majesty meet the Chu crisis without changing course and know disaster will not end—they will surely rise in revolt together.

sentences.zh: 此時即盡戮諸珰以謝天下，寧有濟耶？」

translations.literal: At that time, even if all the eunuchs were slaughtered to appease under Heaven, would there be any help?
translations.idiomatic: By then, even if every eunuch were executed to appease the realm, would it help at all?

sentences.zh: 帝怒，留中。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and retained it in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and withheld the memorial in the palace.

sentences.zh: 又明年遷兵科都給事中。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Military Section.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Chief Supervising Secretary of the Military Section.

sentences.zh: 時兩京缺尚書三，侍郎十、科道九十四，天下缺巡撫三、布按監司六十六、知府二十五。

translations.literal: At the time the two capitals lacked three ministers, ten vice ministers, and ninety-four censorate and supervising-secretary posts; under Heaven lacked three grand coordinators, sixty-six provincial, surveillance, and circuit commissioners, and twenty-five prefects.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the two capitals lacked three ministers, ten vice ministers, and ninety-four censorate and supervising-secretary posts; across the empire three grand coordinators, sixty-six provincial and circuit officials, and twenty-five prefects stood vacant.

sentences.zh: 大益力請簡補，亦不聽。

translations.literal: Dayi strenuously requested selection and filling; this too was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Dayi urgently pleaded that these posts be filled, but was ignored.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，江西稅監潘相請勘合符牒勿經郵傳。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year the Jiangxi tax commissioner Pan Xiang requested that inspection tallies and documents not pass through the postal relay.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-one the Jiangxi tax agent Pan Xiang asked that his tallies and documents bypass the postal relay.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史吳達可駁之，不聽。

translations.literal: The touring censor Wu Dake rebutted it; he was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Touring censor Wu Dake objected, but was overruled.

sentences.zh: 大益復守故事力爭，竟如相請。

translations.literal: Dayi again upheld precedent and strove in opposition, but in the end it was as Xiang requested.
translations.idiomatic: Dayi again fought to uphold precedent, but in the end Pan Xiang got his way.

sentences.zh: 內使王朝嘗言，近京采煤歲可獲銀五千，乃率京營兵劫掠西山諸處。

translations.literal: The inner envoy Wang Chao once said that coal mining near the capital could yield five thousand taels of silver yearly; he then led capital-garrison troops to plunder various places on the Western Hills.
translations.idiomatic: The palace envoy Wang Chao claimed that coal mining near the capital could yield five thousand taels a year, then led capital-garrison troops to plunder the Western Hills.

sentences.zh: 煤戶洶洶，朝以沮撓聞。

translations.literal: The coal households were in uproar; Chao reported obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: The coal miners rose in uproar, and Wang Chao reported that they were obstructing him.

sentences.zh: 有旨逮治，皆入都城訴失業狀。

translations.literal: An order was issued to seize and punish them; all entered the capital city to plead their state of lost livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered their arrest, and they all marched into the capital to plead that they had been driven out of work.

sentences.zh: 沈一貫等急請罷朝，且擬敕諭撫按，未得命。

translations.literal: Shen Yiguan and others urgently requested dismissal of court, and also drafted an edict to instruct the grand coordinator and regional inspector, but did not obtain approval.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yiguan and others urgently asked to adjourn court and drafted an edict for the provincial authorities, but received no approval.

sentences.zh: 大益言：「國家大柄，莫重於兵。

translations.literal: Dayi said: "Of the state's great handles, none is heavier than arms.
translations.idiomatic: Dayi wrote: "Of all the instruments of state, none is heavier than military power.

sentences.zh: 朝擅役禁軍，請急誅，為無將之戒。」

translations.literal: Chao presumptuously employed forbidden troops; I request urgent execution as a warning against commanders without discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chao has dared to command the forbidden troops—execute him at once as a warning to any commander who forgets discipline.

sentences.zh: 御史沈正隆、給事中楊應文、白瑜亦疏諫。

translations.literal: The censor Shen Zhenglong and the supervising secretaries Yang Yingwen and Bai Yu also memorialized in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Shen Zhenglong and supervising secretaries Yang Yingwen and Bai Yu also remonstrated in memorials.

sentences.zh: 帝俱不納。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted none of them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected them all.

sentences.zh: 俄用中官陳永壽奏，乃召朝還。

translations.literal: Before long, following the memorial of the eunuch Chen Yongshou, Chao was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, on the memorial of the eunuch Chen Yongshou, Wang Chao was recalled.

sentences.zh: 遼東稅監高淮擁精騎數百至都城。

translations.literal: The Liaodong tax commissioner Gao Huai led several hundred elite horsemen to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Liaodong tax agent Gao Huai marched several hundred elite horsemen into the capital.

sentences.zh: 大益言：「祖制，人臣不得弄兵。

translations.literal: Dayi said: "By ancestral regulation, subjects must not play with arms.
translations.idiomatic: Dayi wrote: "By ancestral regulation, no subject may wield troops.

sentences.zh: 淮本掃除之役，敢盜兵權，包禍心，罪當誅。」

translations.literal: Huai was originally a sweeping servant; he dared steal military authority and harbors a treacherous heart—his crime deserves execution.
translations.idiomatic: Huai is a menial servant who has dared seize military authority and harbors treasonous intent—his crime deserves death.

sentences.zh: 帝亦不問。

translations.literal: The emperor also did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took no action.

sentences.zh: 明年八月，極陳君德缺失，言：「陛下專誌財利，自私藏外，絕不措意。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the next year he argued to the utmost about the ruler's virtue and its lacks, saying: "Your Majesty concentrates his will on wealth and profit, selfishly hoarding outside, and gives no thought at all.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the following year he laid out the emperor's moral failures at length: "Your Majesty cares only for profit, hoarding wealth in private treasuries and giving no thought to anything else.

sentences.zh: 中外群工，因而泄泄。

translations.literal: Officials within and without the court thereby grew slack.
translations.idiomatic: Officials inside and outside court have grown slack in turn.

sentences.zh: 君臣上下，曾無一念及民。

translations.literal: Ruler and ministers above and below have never had a single thought reaching to the people.
translations.idiomatic: From throne to lowest clerk, not one thought has reached the people.

sentences.zh: 空言相蒙，人怨天怒，妖祲變異，罔不畢集。

translations.literal: Empty words deceive one another; men resent and Heaven rages; omens, vapors, and strange transformations—none fail to gather together.
translations.idiomatic: Empty phrases deceive one another while men resent and Heaven rages; omens and strange transformations gather without end.

sentences.zh: 乃至皇陵為發祥之祖而災，孝陵為創業之祖而災，長陵為奠鼎之祖而亦災。

translations.literal: It reached the point that the imperial tombs of the founding ancestor of auspicious rise suffered disaster, the Xiaoling of the founding-work ancestor suffered disaster, and the Changling of the ancestor who fixed the tripod also suffered disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster has even struck the tomb of the dynastic founder, the tomb of the founding emperor, and the tomb of the emperor who secured the throne.

sentences.zh: 天欲蹶我國家，章章明矣。

translations.literal: Heaven wishes to trip up our state—the signs are brilliantly clear.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven plainly intends to overturn our state.

sentences.zh: 臣觀十餘年來，亂政亟行，不可枚舉，而病源止在貨利一念。

translations.literal: Your servant observes that over more than ten years misrule has been urgently practiced, beyond enumeration, yet the source of the disease lies only in the single thought of goods and profit.
translations.idiomatic: I have watched more than ten years of misrule too numerous to list, yet the disease has only one source: the obsession with profit.

sentences.zh: 今聖諭補缺官矣，釋系囚矣，然礦稅不撤，而群小猶恣橫，閭閻猶朘削，則百工之展布實難，而罪罟之羅織必眾。

translations.literal: Now the sage edicts have filled vacant offices and released bound prisoners, yet mining taxes are not withdrawn, petty men still run rampant, and lanes and wards are still pared down—then the hundred offices' unfolding is truly hard, and the nets of guilt and punishment must be many.
translations.idiomatic: Your recent edicts have filled vacant offices and released prisoners, yet mining levies remain, petty men still run rampant, and neighborhoods are still stripped bare—so honest officials can scarcely work and the nets of punishment only multiply.

sentences.zh: 缺官雖補，系囚雖釋，曾何益哉！

translations.literal: Though vacant offices are filled and bound prisoners released, what benefit is there!
translations.idiomatic: Filling offices and freeing prisoners—what good does it do!

sentences.zh: 陛下中歲以來，所以掩聰明之質，而甘蹈貪愚暴亂之行者，止為家計耳。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty's middle years, the reason he has covered his bright nature and willingly trod the path of greed, folly, violence, and disorder is only household accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty's middle years, the reason you have buried your bright nature and willingly pursued greed, folly, violence, and disorder is simply household accounts.

sentences.zh: 不知家之盈者國必喪。

translations.literal: He does not know that when the household is full, the state must perish.
translations.idiomatic: You do not see that when the household grows full, the state must perish.

sentences.zh: 如夏桀隕於瑤臺，商紂焚於寶玉，幽、厲啟戎於榮夷，桓、靈絕統於私鬻，德宗召難於瓊林，道君兆禍於花石。

translations.literal: Like Xia Jie falling at the Jade Terrace, Shang Zhou burning amid precious jade, You and Li raising Rong and Yi, Huan and Ling ending the succession in private sale, Dezong summoning disaster at the Jade Forest, and Emperor Huizong of Song presaging calamity in Flower-and-Stone.
translations.idiomatic: Jie of Xia fell at the Jade Terrace; Zhou of Shang burned amid his treasures; You and Li of Zhou raised disaster through Rong Yi; Huan and Ling of Han ended their lines through private sales; Dezong of Tang summoned disaster at the Jade Forest; Huizong of Song foreshadowed ruin through his Flower-and-Stone scheme.

sentences.zh: 覆轍相仍，昭然可鑒。

translations.literal: Overturned tracks follow one another—brilliantly they may be mirrored.
translations.idiomatic: These overturned tracks follow one another in plain sight.

sentences.zh: 陛下邇來亂政，不減六代之季。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's recent misrule is no less than the final years of the Six Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's recent misrule rivals the last days of the Six Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 一旦變生，其何以托身於天下哉！」

translations.literal: Once change arises, how will he lodge his person within under Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: When crisis comes, where will Your Majesty find refuge under Heaven!

sentences.zh: 居月餘，復以星變乞固根本，設防禦，罷礦稅。

translations.literal: After more than a month he again, because of stellar change, begged to secure the root foundation, set defenses, and abolish mining taxes.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he again pleaded, citing celestial omens, to secure the dynasty's foundations, strengthen defenses, and abolish mining levies.

sentences.zh: 帝皆不省。

translations.literal: The emperor took notice of none of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 又明年，以久次添註太常少卿，卒官。

translations.literal: The next year, by long seniority he was added and appointed Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, by seniority he was appointed Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and died in office.

sentences.zh: 大益性骨鯁，守官無他營。

translations.literal: Dayi's nature was stern as bone; in holding office he had no other pursuits.
translations.idiomatic: Dayi was unyielding by nature and pursued no private ends in office.

sentences.zh: 數進危言，卒獲免禍。

translations.literal: He several times advanced stern words, yet in the end escaped calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke harsh truth repeatedly yet in the end escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 蓋時帝倦勤，上章者雖千萬言，大率屏置勿閱故也。

translations.literal: This was because at the time the emperor was weary of diligence; though memorialists wrote millions of words, for the most part they were screened aside and not read.
translations.idiomatic: This was because the emperor had grown weary of governing; though memorials ran to millions of words, they were usually set aside unread.

sentences.zh: 馮應京，字可大，盱眙人。

translations.literal: Feng Yingjing, courtesy name Kedà, was a man of Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yingjing, whose courtesy name was Kedà, came from Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十年進士。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twentieth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 為戶部主事。

translations.literal: He served as a director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 督薊鎮軍儲，以廉幹聞。

translations.literal: He supervised military stores of the Ji garrison, and was known for integrity and efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising military stores for the Ji garrison, he became known for integrity and efficiency.

sentences.zh: 尋改兵部，進員外郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to the Ministry of War and advanced to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Ministry of War and promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，擢湖廣僉事，分巡武昌、漢陽、黃州三府。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of Huguang, with divided inspection of the three prefectures Wuchang, Hanyang, and Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-eight he was made Huguang vice commissioner with touring authority over Wuchang, Hanyang, and Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 繩貪墨，摧奸豪，風采大著。

translations.literal: He restrained the greedy and corrupt, crushed villainous magnates, and his presence was greatly manifest.
translations.idiomatic: He punished corruption, crushed local bullies, and made his authority widely felt.

sentences.zh: 稅監陳奉恣橫，巡撫支可大以下唯諾惟謹，應京獨以法裁之。

translations.literal: The tax commissioner Chen Feng was overbearing; the grand coordinator Zhi Kedà and those below only assented with utmost deference, while Yingjing alone judged him by law.
translations.idiomatic: Tax agent Chen Feng ran rampant; Grand Coordinator Zhi Kedà and his subordinates only nodded assent, while Yingjing alone held him to the law.

sentences.zh: 奉掊克萬端，至伐冢毀屋，刳孕婦，溺嬰兒。

translations.literal: Feng extorted in countless ways, reaching the point of felling tombs and destroying houses, cutting open pregnant women, and drowning infants.
translations.idiomatic: Feng extorted by every imaginable means, even tearing down tombs and houses, cutting open pregnant women, and drowning infants.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，有諸生妻被辱，訴上官。

translations.literal: That year in the twelfth month, a licentiate's wife was insulted and appealed to superiors.
translations.idiomatic: That December a student's wife was assaulted and appealed to higher authorities.

sentences.zh: 市民從者萬餘，哭聲動地，蜂湧入奉廨，諸司馳救乃免。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand townspeople followed; weeping shook the earth as they swarmed into Feng's office, and only when various offices rushed to rescue was he spared.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand townspeople followed, their wailing shaking the ground as they stormed Feng's office; only when officials rushed in was he spared.

sentences.zh: 應京捕治其爪牙，奉怒，陽餉食而置金其中。

translations.literal: Yingjing arrested and punished his henchmen; Feng was angry and outwardly offered food while placing gold within it.
translations.idiomatic: Yingjing arrested his henchmen; Feng grew furious and pretended to offer food while hiding gold inside the gift.

sentences.zh: 應京復暴之，益慚恨。

translations.literal: Yingjing again exposed it, and Feng grew still more ashamed and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Yingjing exposed the bribe publicly, deepening Feng's shame and hatred.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，置酒邀諸司，以甲士千人自衛，遂舉火箭焚民居。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year he set out wine and invited the various offices, guarded himself with a thousand armored soldiers, and then raised fire-arrows to burn common dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: The following January he held a banquet for the local offices, surrounded himself with a thousand armored guards, and then fired rockets to burn civilian homes.

sentences.zh: 民群擁奉門。

translations.literal: The people in crowds besieged Feng's gate.
translations.idiomatic: The people massed at Feng's gate.

sentences.zh: 奉遣人擊之，多死，碎其屍，擲諸途。

translations.literal: Feng sent men to strike them; many died, their corpses were smashed, and cast upon the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Feng sent men to attack them; many were killed, their bodies mutilated and thrown into the streets.

sentences.zh: 可大噤不敢出聲，應京獨抗疏列其十大罪。

translations.literal: Kedà was silenced and dared not speak; Yingjing alone submitted a defiant memorial listing Feng's ten great crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Kedà fell silent and dared not speak out, while Yingjing alone filed a bold memorial listing Feng's ten great crimes.

sentences.zh: 奉亦誣奏應京撓命，陵敕使。

translations.literal: Feng also falsely memorialized that Yingjing obstructed orders and insulted the edict-envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Feng also falsely accused Yingjing of obstructing orders and insulting the imperial envoy.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命貶雜職，調邊方。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered him demoted to miscellaneous office and transferred to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered Yingjing demoted to a minor post on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 給事中田大益、御史李以唐等交章劾奉，乞宥應京。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries Tian Dayi and Li Yitang and others submitted memorials one after another impeaching Feng and begging pardon for Yingjing.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Tian Dayi and censor Li Yitang and others filed memorial after memorial impeaching Feng and pleading for Yingjing's pardon.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，除應京名。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still angrier and struck Yingjing's name from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor only grew angrier and struck Yingjing from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 是時，襄陽通判邸宅、推官何棟如、棗陽縣知縣王之翰亦忤奉被劾。

translations.literal: At this time the Xiangyang assistant prefect Di Zhai, investigating censor He Dongru, and Zaoyang magistrate Wang Zhihan also offended Feng and were impeached.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Xiangyang assistant prefect Di Zhai, investigating censor He Dongru, and Zaoyang magistrate Wang Zhihan had also crossed Feng and were impeached.

sentences.zh: 詔宅、之翰為民，棟如遣逮。

translations.literal: An edict made Zhai and Zhihan commoners; Dongru was ordered seized.
translations.idiomatic: An edict reduced Zhai and Zhihan to commoner status and ordered Dongru arrested.

sentences.zh: 俄以都給事中楊應文論救，遂並逮應京、宅、之翰三人。

translations.literal: Before long, because Chief Supervising Secretary Yang Yingwen argued in defense, Yingjing, Zhai, and Zhihan were all seized together.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, after Chief Supervising Secretary Yang Yingwen pleaded for mercy, Yingjing, Zhai, and Zhihan were all arrested together.

sentences.zh: 頃之，奉又誣劾武昌同知卞孔時抗拒，孔時亦被逮。

translations.literal: Before long Feng again falsely impeached Wuchang assistant prefect Bian Kongshi for resistance; Kongshi was also seized.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Feng also falsely accused Wuchang assistant prefect Bian Kongshi of resistance, and Kongshi was arrested as well.

sentences.zh: 緹騎抵武昌，民知應京獲重譴，相率痛哭。

translations.literal: The imperial guards arrived at Wuchang; the people, knowing Yingjing had received heavy punishment, followed one another in bitter weeping.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial guards reached Wuchang, the people learned that Yingjing faced severe punishment and wept together in the streets.

sentences.zh: 奉乃大書應京名，列其罪，榜之通衢。

translations.literal: Feng then wrote Yingjing's name in large characters, listed his crimes, and posted them on the main thoroughfare.
translations.idiomatic: Feng then posted Yingjing's name in large characters on the main thoroughfare, listing his supposed crimes.

sentences.zh: 士民益憤，聚數萬人圍奉廨，奉窘，逃匿楚王府，遂執其斥牙六人，投之江，並傷緹騎；

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners grew still angrier; tens of thousands gathered and besieged Feng's office; Feng was cornered, fled and hid in the Chu princely residence, then seized six of his henchmen and cast them into the river, also wounding the imperial guards;
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and commoners grew furious; tens of thousands besieged Feng's office; cornered, Feng fled into the Prince of Chu's residence; the crowd seized six of his henchmen, threw them into the river, and wounded several imperial guards;

sentences.zh: 詈可大助虐，焚其府門，可大不敢出。

translations.literal: they cursed Kedà for aiding tyranny, burned his prefectural gate, and Kedà dared not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: they cursed Kedà for aiding the tyranny, burned his prefectural gate, and Kedà dared not come out.

sentences.zh: 奉潛遣參隨三百人，引兵追逐，射殺數人，傷者不可勝計。

translations.literal: Feng secretly sent three hundred attendants, led troops in pursuit, shot and killed several persons, and the wounded were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Feng secretly sent three hundred attendants with troops in pursuit, killing several and wounding more than could be counted.

sentences.zh: 日已晡，猶紛。

translations.literal: The sun had already passed the hour of shen, yet turmoil continued.
translations.idiomatic: By late afternoon the turmoil still had not ended.

sentences.zh: 應京囚服坐檻車，曉以大義，乃稍稍解散。

translations.literal: Yingjing in prisoner's garb sat in the caged cart and enlightened them with great principle; only then did they slowly disperse.
translations.idiomatic: Yingjing, dressed as a prisoner in the caged cart, reasoned with them on principle, and only then did the crowd slowly disperse.

sentences.zh: 奉匿楚府，逾月不敢出，亟請還京。

translations.literal: Feng hid in the Chu residence; for more than a month he dared not emerge and urgently requested return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Feng hid in the Chu princely residence for more than a month without daring to emerge and urgently begged to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 大學士沈一貫因極言奉罪，請立代還。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan thereupon argued to the utmost about Feng's crimes and requested that a replacement be immediately sent and Feng recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan laid out Feng's crimes at length and asked that a replacement be sent at once to recall him.

sentences.zh: 言官亦爭以為請。

translations.literal: Censors also contended in making the request.
translations.idiomatic: Censors also pressed the same request.

sentences.zh: 帝未許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 俄江西稅監李道亦奏奉侵匿狀，乃召還，隸其事於承天守備杜茂。

translations.literal: Before long the Jiangxi tax commissioner Li Dao also memorialized Feng's embezzlement and concealment; then he was recalled, and his affairs were placed under the Chengdu garrison commander Du Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Jiangxi tax agent Li Dao also reported Feng's embezzlement; Feng was recalled and his affairs were handed to Chengdu garrison commander Du Mao.

sentences.zh: 頃之，東廠奏緹騎有死者。

translations.literal: Before long the Eastern Depot reported that imperial guards had died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Eastern Depot reported that imperial guards had been killed.

sentences.zh: 帝慍甚，手詔內閣，欲究主謀。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly displeased and by hand-edict to the Grand Secretariat wished to investigate the chief plotter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and by personal edict to the Grand Secretariat demanded investigation of the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 一貫言民心宜靜，請亟遣重臣代可大拊循，因以侍郎趙可懷薦。

translations.literal: Yiguan said the people's hearts ought to be calmed and urgently requested dispatch of a weighty minister to replace Kedà in soothing them, recommending Vice Minister Zhao Kehuai for the purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan urged that popular feeling must be calmed and asked that a senior minister be sent at once to replace Kedà and pacify the region, recommending Vice Minister Zhao Kehuai.

sentences.zh: 帝乃褫可大官，令可懷馳往。

translations.literal: The emperor then stripped Kedà of office and ordered Kehuai to hurry there.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stripped Kedà of office and ordered Kehuai to hurry to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 未至，可大已遣兵護奉行。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Kedà had already sent troops to escort Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Before Kehuai arrived, Kedà had already sent troops to escort Feng.

sentences.zh: 舟車相銜，數里不絕。

translations.literal: Boats and carts linked one to another for several li without end.
translations.idiomatic: Boats and carts stretched for miles without a break.

sentences.zh: 可懷入境，亦遣使護之。

translations.literal: When Kehuai entered the territory, he also dispatched envoys to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: When Kehuai entered the province, he too sent escorts for Feng.

sentences.zh: 奉得迄邐去。

translations.literal: Feng was able to depart at last in leisurely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was able to leave at last in safety.

sentences.zh: 應京之就逮也，士民擁檻車號哭，車不得行。

translations.literal: When Yingjing was seized, gentry and commoners surrounded the caged cart wailing; the cart could not move.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingjing was taken, gentry and commoners surrounded his cart wailing so that it could not move.

sentences.zh: 既去，則家為位祀之。

translations.literal: After he had gone, households set up places to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: After he was gone, families set up shrines to honor him.

sentences.zh: 三郡父老相率詣闕訴冤，帝不省。

translations.literal: Elders of the three prefectures followed one another to the palace gates to plead injustice; the emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: Elders from the three prefectures marched to the capital to plead injustice, but the emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 吏科都給事中郭如星、刑科給事中陳維春更連章劾奉。

translations.literal: Chief Supervising Secretary Guo Ruxing of the Personnel Section and Chen Weichun of the Punishments Section again submitted memorials in succession impeaching Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Supervising Secretary Guo Ruxing and supervising secretary Chen Weichun filed memorial after memorial impeaching Feng.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，謫兩人邊方雜職，系應京等詔獄，拷訊久之不釋。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, demoted the two to miscellaneous posts on the frontier, imprisoned Yingjing and others in the imperial prison, and interrogated under torture for a long time without release.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, banished the two to minor frontier posts, threw Yingjing and the others into the imperial prison, and tortured them for months without release.

sentences.zh: 應京乃於獄中著書，昕夕無倦。

translations.literal: Yingjing then composed books in prison, morning and evening without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Yingjing wrote books in prison from morning to night without rest.

sentences.zh: 三十二年九月，星變修省。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the thirty-second year, because of stellar change he cultivated self-examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year thirty-two, celestial omens prompted the court to examine itself.

sentences.zh: 廷臣多請釋系囚，於是應京及宅、棟如獲釋。

translations.literal: Court ministers mostly requested release of bound prisoners; thereupon Yingjing, Zhai, and Dongru obtained release.
translations.idiomatic: Many court officials pleaded for the release of prisoners; Yingjing, Zhai, and Dongru were then freed.

sentences.zh: 之翰先瘐死，而孔時系獄如故。

translations.literal: Zhihan had earlier died of illness in confinement, while Kongshi remained imprisoned as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhihan had already died in prison from illness, while Kongshi remained imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 應京誌操卓犖，學求有用，不事空言，為淮西士人之冠。

translations.literal: Yingjing's will and conduct were outstanding; in learning he sought what was useful and did not pursue empty words—he was chief among the gentry scholars of west Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Yingjing's integrity was outstanding; he sought learning that could be put to use and scorned empty talk, standing at the head of Huai River scholars.

sentences.zh: 出獄三年卒。

translations.literal: Three years after leaving prison he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died three years after his release.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，贈太常少卿，謚恭節。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, with posthumous title Gongjie.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianqi reign he was posthumously made Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices with the posthumous title Gongjie, "Respectful Integrity."

sentences.zh: 何棟如，無錫人。

translations.literal: He Dongru was a man of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: He Dongru came from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 居官守正。

translations.literal: In holding office he upheld rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: In office he upheld rectitude.

sentences.zh: 既為奉所陷，襄陽人赴闕訴冤，不聽。

translations.literal: After he was trapped by Feng, the people of Xiangyang went to the palace gates to plead injustice; they were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: After Feng had framed him, the people of Xiangyang went to the capital to plead injustice, but were ignored.

sentences.zh: 及出獄，削籍歸，家居十七年。

translations.literal: When he left prison he was struck from the rolls and returned home, living at home seventeen years.
translations.idiomatic: After his release he was struck from the rolls and lived at home for seventeen years.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，始起南京兵部主事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was first raised as director in the Nanjing Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianqi he was first recalled as a director in the Nanjing Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 會遼陽陷，時議募兵，棟如自請行。

translations.literal: When Liaoyang fell, the time's discussion was to recruit troops; Dongru volunteered to go.
translations.idiomatic: When Liaoyang fell and the court debated recruiting troops, Dongru volunteered to go.

sentences.zh: 遂賫帑金赴浙江，得六千七百人。

translations.literal: He then carried treasury funds to Zhejiang and obtained six thousand seven hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: He carried treasury funds to Zhejiang and raised six thousand seven hundred men.

sentences.zh: 甫至而廣寧復陷，又自請出關視形勢。

translations.literal: He had just arrived when Guangning again fell; he again volunteered to go beyond the pass to observe the situation.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely arrived when Guangning fell again; he again volunteered to go beyond the pass to survey conditions.

sentences.zh: 乃進太僕少卿，充軍前贊畫。

translations.literal: He was then advanced to Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud and served as staff planner before the army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud and made a staff planner with the army.

sentences.zh: 棟如誌銳而才疏。

translations.literal: Dongru's will was sharp but his talent sparse.
translations.idiomatic: Dongru was bold in spirit but limited in talent.

sentences.zh: 初在浙，不能無浮費。

translations.literal: At first in Zhejiang he could not be without wasteful spending.
translations.idiomatic: Early on in Zhejiang he could not avoid wasteful spending.

sentences.zh: 所募兵畏出關，多逃亡。

translations.literal: The troops he recruited feared going beyond the pass and many fled.
translations.idiomatic: The troops he recruited feared crossing the pass and many deserted.

sentences.zh: 及兩疏論熊廷弼、王化貞功罪，給事中蔡思充、朱童蒙，御史陳保泰遂交章劾之。

translations.literal: When he submitted two memorials discussing the merits and crimes of Xiong Tingbi and Wang Huazhen, the supervising secretaries Cai Sichong and Zhu Tongmeng and the censor Chen Baotai then submitted memorials one after another impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: When he filed two memorials on the merits and faults of Xiong Tingbi and Wang Huazhen, supervising secretaries Cai Sichong and Zhu Tongmeng and censor Chen Baotai impeached him in turn.

sentences.zh: 棟如疏辨，因請非時考察京官，用清朋黨。

translations.literal: Dongru memorialized in defense and thereupon requested out-of-season inspection of capital officials to clear factional cliques.
translations.idiomatic: Dongru defended himself and asked for an extraordinary review of capital officials to purge factional cliques.

sentences.zh: 朝貴大恨，遂下詔獄，榜掠備至。

translations.literal: Court magnates hated this greatly; he was then thrown into the imperial prison and flogged to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Court magnates hated this deeply; he was thrown into the imperial prison and tortured without mercy.

sentences.zh: 五年秋，坐贓戍滁陽。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year he was punished for corruption and exiled to guard Chuyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifth year he was convicted of corruption and exiled to Chuyang.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，復官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chongzhen reign his office was restored.

sentences.zh: 致仕卒。

translations.literal: He retired and died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired and died.

sentences.zh: 王之翰，絳州人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhihan was a man of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhihan came from Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 官棗陽。

translations.literal: He served as official of Zaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Zaoyang.

sentences.zh: 力阻開礦，遂被逮拷死。

translations.literal: He strenuously blocked opening mines and was therefore seized, tortured, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He fought hard against opening mines, was arrested, tortured, and died.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianqi he was posthumously made Vice Minister of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 孔時既長系，廷臣救者數十上。

translations.literal: Since Kongshi had long been imprisoned, court ministers who rescued him submitted dozens of memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Kongshi had been imprisoned for a long time, and dozens of court officials memorialized for his release.

sentences.zh: 帝皆不省。

translations.literal: The emperor took notice of none.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored them all.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，萬壽節，葉向高復以為言，乃削籍放還。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, on the Longevity Festival, Ye Xianggao again spoke on his behalf; only then was he struck from the rolls and released to return.
translations.idiomatic: In year forty-one, on the imperial birthday, Ye Xianggao spoke for him again, and Kongshi was struck from the rolls and sent home.

sentences.zh: 熹宗立，起南京刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong ascended, he was raised as vice director in the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong took the throne, he was recalled as vice director in the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 吳宗堯，字仁叔，歙縣人。

translations.literal: Wu Zongyao, courtesy name Renshu, was a man of She County.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zongyao, whose courtesy name was Renshu, came from She County.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十三年進士。
