translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twenty-third year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 授益都知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 性強項。

translations.literal: His nature was strong and unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: He was unyielding by nature.

sentences.zh: 中官陳增以開礦至，誣奏福山知縣韋國賢阻撓，被逮削籍。

translations.literal: The eunuch Chen Zeng came for opening mines and falsely memorialized that Fushan magistrate Wei Guoxian obstructed him; he was seized and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Chen Zeng came to open mines, he falsely accused Fushan magistrate Wei Guoxian of obstruction; Guoxian was arrested and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 守令多屈節如屬吏，宗堯獨具賓主禮。

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates mostly bent their integrity like subordinate officials; Zongyao alone treated him with host-and-guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Most local officials bowed to him like subordinates; Zongyao alone treated him with the ceremony due between host and guest.

sentences.zh: 增黨程守訓，宗堯邑子也。

translations.literal: Zeng's partisan Cheng Shouxun was a fellow townsman of Zongyao.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng's henchman Cheng Shouxun was a fellow townsman of Zongyao.

sentences.zh: 宗堯惡其奸，不與通。

translations.literal: Zongyao detested his treachery and did not associate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyao detested his treachery and refused all contact.

sentences.zh: 驛丞金子登說增開孟丘山礦，宗堯叱其欺罔。

translations.literal: The post-station assistant Jin Zideng urged Zeng to open the Mengqiu Mountain mine; Zongyao rebuked him for deception.
translations.idiomatic: Post-station assistant Jin Zideng urged Zeng to open the Mengqiu Mountain mine; Zongyao denounced the scheme as fraudulent.

sentences.zh: 子登懼，構於增。

translations.literal: Zideng was afraid and framed Zongyao before Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zideng grew afraid and framed Zongyao before Zeng.

sentences.zh: 日征千人鑿山，多捶死；

translations.literal: Daily a thousand men were levied to dig the mountain, and many were beaten to death;
translations.idiomatic: A thousand men were levied daily to dig the mountain, and many were beaten to death;

sentences.zh: 又誣富民盜礦，三日捕系五百人。

translations.literal: they also falsely accused wealthy households of stealing ore, and in three days seized and bound five hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: wealthy households were also falsely accused of stealing ore, and five hundred people were arrested in three days.

sentences.zh: 二十六年九月，宗堯盡發增不法事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-sixth year Zongyao fully exposed Zeng's unlawful acts.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year twenty-six Zongyao exposed all of Zeng's unlawful acts.

sentences.zh: 帝得疏意動，持不下。

translations.literal: The emperor, receiving the memorial, was moved in mind and held it without issuing it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved by the memorial but withheld action.

sentences.zh: 會給事中包見捷極論增罪，請撤還。

translations.literal: It happened that supervising secretary Bao Jianjie argued to the utmost about Zeng's crimes and requested withdrawal and recall.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Bao Jianjie then argued at length against Zeng's crimes and asked that he be recalled.

sentences.zh: 帝責增，令檢下。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Zeng and ordered him to turn in his tallies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Zeng and ordered him to surrender his credentials.

sentences.zh: 見捷同官郝敬復請治增罪，帝乃不悅，責宗堯狂逞要名。

translations.literal: Jianjie's colleague Hao Jing again requested punishment of Zeng's crimes; the emperor then was displeased and rebuked Zongyao for wild arrogance seeking fame.
translations.idiomatic: Jianjie's colleague Hao Jing again asked that Zeng be punished; the emperor grew displeased and rebuked Zongyao for reckless grandstanding.

sentences.zh: 已而山東巡撫尹應元劾增背旨虐民二十罪。

translations.literal: Before long Shandong grand coordinator Yin Yingyuan impeached Zeng for twenty crimes of defying the edict and abusing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shandong grand coordinator Yin Yingyuan impeached Zeng for twenty crimes of defying the throne and abusing the people.

sentences.zh: 帝遂發怒，切責應元，削宗堯籍。

translations.literal: The emperor then burst into anger, sharply rebuked Yingyuan, and struck Zongyao from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, sharply rebuked Yingyuan, and struck Zongyao from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 敬復抗疏諫，帝益怒，奪俸一年，並奪應元俸。

translations.literal: Jing again submitted a defiant memorial in remonstrance; the emperor grew still angrier, stripped one year's salary, and also stripped Yingyuan's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Jing remonstrated again in a bold memorial; the emperor grew angrier, suspended his salary for a year, and suspended Yingyuan's salary as well.

sentences.zh: 增遂劾宗堯阻撓礦務，且令守訓誣訐之。

translations.literal: Zeng then impeached Zongyao for obstructing mining affairs and also had Shouxun falsely accuse and denounce him.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng then impeached Zongyao for obstructing mining operations and had Shouxun lodge false accusations against him.

sentences.zh: 帝既遣逮治，御史劉景辰、給事中侯慶遠爭之，不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor had already dispatched orders to seize and punish him; censor Liu Jingchen and supervising secretary Hou Qingyuan contended on his behalf, but were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already ordered his arrest; censor Liu Jingchen and supervising secretary Hou Qingyuan protested, but were ignored.

sentences.zh: 使者至，民大嘩，欲殺增。

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived, the people were in great uproar and wished to kill Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: When the arresting party arrived, the people rose in uproar and wanted to kill Zeng.

sentences.zh: 宗堯行，民哭聲震地。

translations.literal: As Zongyao departed, the people's weeping shook the earth.
translations.idiomatic: As Zongyao was led away, the people's wailing shook the ground.

sentences.zh: 既至，下詔獄拷訊，系經年。

translations.literal: After he arrived, he was thrown into the imperial prison for interrogation under torture and imprisoned for more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: After he reached the capital he was thrown into the imperial prison, tortured, and held for more than a year.

sentences.zh: 禮部郎鮑應鰲等言於沈一貫曰：「南康守吳寶秀已得安居牖下，宗堯何獨不然？」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites clerk Bao Ying'ao and others said to Shen Yiguan: "The Nankang prefect Wu Baoxiu has already been able to dwell peacefully beneath his window—why should Zongyao alone not be so?
translations.idiomatic: Ministry of Rites clerk Bao Ying'ao and others said to Shen Yiguan: "Nankang prefect Wu Baoxiu has already been allowed to live peacefully at home—why should Zongyao alone be treated differently?

sentences.zh: 一貫揭入，即釋為民，未幾卒。

translations.literal: Yiguan presented it to the throne, and he was immediately released as a commoner; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan presented the plea to the throne, and Zongyao was immediately released; he died not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 天啟時，贈光祿少卿，賜祭，錄一子。

translations.literal: During Tianqi he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, given sacrificial rites, and one son was enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi he was posthumously made Vice Minister of Imperial Entertainments, granted state sacrifices, and one son was enrolled in office.

sentences.zh: 吳寶秀，字汝珍，平陽人。

translations.literal: Wu Baoxiu, courtesy name Ruzhen, was a man of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Baoxiu, whose courtesy name was Ruzhen, came from Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十七年進士。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the seventeenth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 授大理評事。

translations.literal: He was appointed reviewer in the Court of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a reviewing official in the Court of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 歷寺正，出為南康知府。

translations.literal: He successively served as director of the court, then went out as prefect of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director of the court, then became prefect of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 湖口稅監李道橫甚，寶秀不與通。

translations.literal: The Hukou tax commissioner Li Dao was very overbearing; Baoxiu did not associate with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Hukou tax agent Li Dao was brutally overbearing, and Baoxiu refused all contact with him.

sentences.zh: 漕舟南還，乘風揚帆入湖口。

translations.literal: Grain-transport boats returning south caught the wind and raised sails to enter Hukou.
translations.idiomatic: Grain boats returning south caught the wind and sailed into Hukou.

sentences.zh: 道欲榷其貨，遣卒急追之，舟覆，有死者。

translations.literal: Dao wished to monopolize-tax their cargo, sent soldiers in urgent pursuit, the boats capsized, and some died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dao tried to tax their cargo, sent soldiers in hot pursuit, the boats capsized, and some men drowned.

sentences.zh: 道遣吏捕漕卒，寶秀拒不發。

translations.literal: Dao sent clerks to arrest the transport soldiers; Baoxiu refused to issue them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dao sent officers to arrest the transport crews, but Baoxiu refused to hand them over.

sentences.zh: 道怒，劾寶秀及星子知縣吳一元、青山巡檢程資阻撓稅務，詔俱逮治。

translations.literal: Dao was angry and impeached Baoxiu, Xingzi magistrate Wu Yiyuan, and Qingshan inspector Cheng Zi for obstructing tax affairs; an edict ordered all seized and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dao grew furious and impeached Baoxiu, Xingzi magistrate Wu Yiyuan, and Qingshan inspector Cheng Zi for obstructing tax collection; an edict ordered all three arrested.

sentences.zh: 給事中楊應文等請下撫按公勘。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Yang Yingwen and others requested that the grand coordinator and regional inspector conduct a public investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Yang Yingwen and others asked that the provincial authorities conduct a joint investigation.

sentences.zh: 大學士沈一貫、吏部尚書李戴、國子祭酒方從哲等交章為言，俱不報。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan, Minister of Personnel Li Dai, National University Chancellor Fang Congzhe, and others submitted memorials one after another on their behalf; none received reply.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan, Minister of Personnel Li Dai, National University Chancellor Fang Congzhe, and others pleaded in memorial after memorial, but none received a response.

sentences.zh: 寶秀妻陳氏慟哭，請偕行，寶秀不可。

translations.literal: Baoxiu's wife, the Chen clan, wept bitterly and asked to go together; Baoxiu would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxiu's wife, Lady Chen, wept bitterly and asked to accompany him; Baoxiu refused.

sentences.zh: 乃括余貲及簪珥付其妾曰：「夫子行，以為路費。」

translations.literal: She then gathered remaining funds and hairpins and earrings, gave them to his concubine, and said: "Our master is going—use these as travel expenses.
translations.idiomatic: She gathered their remaining money and her jewelry, gave them to his concubine, and said: "Your master is leaving—use these for his travel expenses.

sentences.zh: 夜自經死。

translations.literal: That night she hanged herself and died.
translations.idiomatic: That night she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 寶秀至京，下詔獄。

translations.literal: When Baoxiu reached the capital he was thrown into the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoxiu reached the capital he was thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 大學士趙誌臯上言：「頃臣臥病，聞中外人情洶洶，皆為礦稅一事。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhao Zhigao submitted: "Recently your servant lay ill and heard that feeling within and without the court was turbulent—all because of the mining-tax matter.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhao Zhigao wrote: "While I was recently ill in bed, I heard that feeling inside and outside court was turbulent—all because of mining levies.

sentences.zh: 南康守吳寶秀逮系時，其妻至投繯自盡，闔郡號呼，幾成變亂。

translations.literal: When Nankang prefect Wu Baoxiu was seized and bound, his wife went so far as to cast a noose and kill herself; the whole prefecture cried out and nearly erupted in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: When Nankang prefect Wu Baoxiu was arrested, his wife hanged herself; the whole prefecture cried out and nearly erupted in revolt.

sentences.zh: 事關民生向背，宗社安危，臣不敢以將去之身，隱默而不言。」

translations.literal: The matter concerns the people's livelihood and where their hearts turn, and the ancestral altars' safety and peril—your servant dares not, with a body about to depart, remain silent and not speak.
translations.idiomatic: This touches the people's livelihood and the safety of the altars of state—I dare not, on the eve of my retirement, remain silent.

sentences.zh: 星子民陳英者，方廬墓，約儒士熊應鳳等走京師，伏闕訟冤，乞以身代。

translations.literal: The Xingzi commoner Chen Ying, who was building a tomb mound, agreed with the scholar Xiong Yingfeng and others to hurry to the capital, prostrate themselves at the palace gates to plead injustice, and beg to substitute their bodies for his.
translations.idiomatic: A Xingzi commoner named Chen Ying, who was building a tomb, joined scholars including Xiong Yingfeng in rushing to the capital, prostrating themselves at the palace gates to plead injustice and offering their lives in Baoxiu's place.

sentences.zh: 於是撫按及南北諸臣論救者疏十餘上，帝皆不省。

translations.literal: Thereupon the grand coordinator, regional inspector, and various ministers north and south who argued for rescue submitted more than ten memorials; the emperor took notice of none.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinators, censors, and officials north and south filed more than ten rescue memorials; the emperor ignored them all.

sentences.zh: 一日，司禮田義匯諸疏進御前，帝怒擲地。

translations.literal: One day the Directorate of Ceremonies' Tian Yi gathered the memorials and presented them before the throne; the emperor angrily threw them to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: One day Directorate of Ceremonies official Tian Yi gathered the memorials and presented them; the emperor angrily threw them to the floor.

sentences.zh: 義從容拾起，復進之，叩首曰：「閣臣跪候朝門外，不奉處分不敢退。」

translations.literal: Yi calmly picked them up, presented them again, and kowtowed saying: "Grand Secretariat ministers kneel waiting outside the court gate; without receiving disposition they dare not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Yi calmly picked them up, presented them again, and kowtowed: "The Grand Secretariat ministers are kneeling outside the court gate; without your decision they dare not leave.

sentences.zh: 帝怒稍平，取閱閣臣疏，命移獄刑部。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger gradually eased; he took and read the Grand Secretariat memorials and ordered the prisoners moved to the Ministry of Punishments prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger eased somewhat; he read the Grand Secretariat memorials and ordered the prisoners transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 皇太后亦聞陳氏之死，從容為帝言。

translations.literal: The empress dowager also heard of the Chen clan woman's death and calmly spoke to the emperor about it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager also heard of Lady Chen's death and spoke calmly to the emperor about it.

sentences.zh: 至九月，與一元等並釋為民。

translations.literal: By the ninth month he and Yiyuan and others were all released as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: By the ninth month he and Yiyuan and the others were all released.

sentences.zh: 歸家，逾年卒。

translations.literal: He returned home and died after more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home and died a little over a year later.

sentences.zh: 初，南康士民建祠，特祀陳氏，後合寶秀祀之。

translations.literal: At first the gentry and commoners of Nankang built a shrine and specially worshipped the Chen clan; later they joined Baoxiu in the worship.
translations.idiomatic: At first the people of Nankang built a shrine to honor Lady Chen alone; later Baoxiu was worshipped there as well.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，贈太僕少卿，賜祭，錄其一子。

translations.literal: During Tianqi he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, given sacrificial rites, and one son was enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi he was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud, granted state sacrifices, and one son was enrolled in office.

sentences.zh: 華鈺，字德夫，丹徒人。

translations.literal: Hua Yu, courtesy name Defu, was a man of Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yu, whose courtesy name was Defu, came from Dantu.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twenty-third year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 授荊州推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 稅監陳奉仆直馳府署中，鈺笞之。

translations.literal: The tax commissioner Chen Feng's servant Puzhi galloped straight into the prefectural office; Yu had him beaten with the bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Tax agent Chen Feng's servant Puzhi galloped straight into the prefectural office; Yu had him flogged.

sentences.zh: 奉佯謝，銜之刺骨。

translations.literal: Feng pretended to apologize but harbored resentment to the bone.
translations.idiomatic: Feng pretended to apologize but nursed a bitter grudge.

sentences.zh: 奉所受敕止江稅，乃故移之市，又倍蓰征之。

translations.literal: The edict Feng received was only for Yangtze taxes, yet he deliberately shifted it to the markets and again levied at several times the rate.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's commission covered only Yangtze taxes, yet he deliberately shifted collection to the markets and doubled and redoubled the levies.

sentences.zh: 稍與辨，輒毆擊破面。

translations.literal: If one argued even slightly, he would beat and strike until the face was broken.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who argued was beaten until his face was broken.

sentences.zh: 商賈怖匿，負擔者不敢出其途。

translations.literal: Merchants were terrified and hid; porters dared not go out on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants hid in terror, and porters dared not travel the roads.

sentences.zh: 鈺白御史嚴戢，奉益恨。

translations.literal: Yu reported to the censor Yan Ji to restrain him; Feng hated this all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Yu reported Feng to censor Yan Ji for restraint; Feng hated him all the more.

sentences.zh: 奉欲榷沙市稅，沙市人群起逐之，奉疑鈺所使。

translations.literal: Feng wished to monopolize-tax Shashi; the people of Shashi rose together to drive him off, and Feng suspected Yu had instigated it.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng tried to tax Shashi, the townspeople rose and drove him out; Feng suspected Yu had instigated them.

sentences.zh: 已，欲榷黃州團風鎮稅，復為鎮民所逐，奉又疑經歷車任重教之。

translations.literal: Later he wished to monopolize-tax Tuanfeng Market in Huangzhou; he was again driven off by the market townspeople, and Feng again suspected the registrar Che Renzhong had taught them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he tried to tax Tuanfeng Market in Huangzhou, the townspeople drove him out again; Feng suspected registrar Che Renzhong had coached them.

sentences.zh: 遂上疏極論鈺、任重阻撓罪，並及巡按御史曹楷、襄陽知府李商耕、黃州知府趙文煥、荊門知州高則巽等數十人。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial arguing to the utmost about the crimes of Yu and Renzhong in obstruction, and implicated touring censor Cao Kai, Xiangyang prefect Li Shanggeng, Huangzhou prefect Zhao Wenhuan, Jingmen prefect Gao Zexun, and several tens of others.
translations.idiomatic: He then filed a memorial charging Yu and Renzhong with obstruction and implicating dozens of officials including touring censor Cao Kai, Xiangyang prefect Li Shanggeng, Huangzhou prefect Zhao Wenhuan, and Jingmen prefect Gao Zexun.

sentences.zh: 帝切責楷，貶商耕等三人官，鈺、任重皆被逮。

translations.literal: The emperor sharply rebuked Kai, demoted Shanggeng and three others in office, and Yu and Renzhong were both seized.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sharply rebuked Cao Kai, demoted Li Shanggeng and two others, and had Yu and Renzhong arrested.

sentences.zh: 時二十七年八月也。

translations.literal: This was the eighth month of the twenty-seventh year.
translations.idiomatic: This was the eighth month of year twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 既至，下鎮撫獄訊治，俾引御史楷。

translations.literal: After they arrived they were thrown into the Embroidered-Uniform Guard prison for interrogation and punishment, and made to implicate Censor Kai.
translations.idiomatic: After they reached the capital they were thrown into the Embroidered-Uniform Guard prison and pressed to implicate Censor Cao Kai.

sentences.zh: 鈺堅不承，系獄中。

translations.literal: Yu firmly would not confess and was bound in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Yu steadfastly refused to confess and remained imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 初，吳宗堯、吳寶秀皆不久即釋。

translations.literal: At first Wu Zongyao and Wu Baoxiu were both released before long.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zongyao and Wu Baoxiu had both been released fairly soon.

sentences.zh: 帝欲痛折辱以懼之，於是鈺與馮應京、王正誌等先後十餘人悉長系。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to break and humiliate them painfully to instill fear; thus Yu, Feng Yingjing, Wang Zhengzhi, and more than ten others in succession were all long imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to break them through harsh imprisonment as a warning; Yu, Feng Yingjing, Wang Zhengzhi, and more than ten others were therefore held for years.

sentences.zh: 廷臣論救章數上，皆不報。

translations.literal: Court ministers' memorials arguing for rescue were submitted several times; none received reply.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials filed repeated pleas for mercy, but none received a response.

sentences.zh: 獄中有鳥，形類鶴而小，怪鳴，則逮者至。

translations.literal: In the prison there was a bird, in form like a crane but small; when it cried strangely, those seized would arrive.
translations.idiomatic: In the prison there was a small crane-like bird; when it cried strangely, a new prisoner would arrive.

sentences.zh: 一夕，鳥鳴甚哀。

translations.literal: One evening the bird cried very mournfully.
translations.idiomatic: One evening the bird cried mournfully.

sentences.zh: 鈺起坐俟之，則應京至。

translations.literal: Yu sat up and waited; then Yingjing arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sat up to wait, and Feng Yingjing was brought in.

sentences.zh: 居久之，語鈺以主靜窮理之學，日相與研究。

translations.literal: After dwelling there a long time, he spoke to Yu of the learning of mastering quiet and exhausting principle, and day by day they studied together.
translations.idiomatic: After a long stay, he taught Yu the Neo-Confucian pursuit of quietude and the investigation of principle, and they studied together every day.

sentences.zh: 三十二年六月，長陵災，肆赦，鈺與任並釋為民。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the thirty-second year the Changling suffered disaster; a general amnesty was proclaimed, and Yu and Ren were both released as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year thirty-two, after disaster struck the Changling tomb, a general amnesty was proclaimed, and Yu and Renzhong were released.

sentences.zh: 家居四年卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home four years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home four years and then died.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，贈尚寶少卿，賜祭，錄一子。

translations.literal: During Tianqi he was posthumously granted Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Seals, given sacrificial rites, and one son was enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Seals, granted state sacrifices, and one son was enrolled in office.

sentences.zh: 王正誌，祥符人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhengzhi was a man of Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhengzhi came from Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十六年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twenty-sixth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 除富平知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Fuping.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Fuping.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，稅使梁永、趙欽肆虐，正誌捕其黨李英，杖殺之，因極論二人不法罪。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the tax agents Liang Yong and Zhao Qin ran rampant; Zhengzhi arrested their partisan Li Ying, beat him to death with the staff, and thereby argued to the utmost about the two men's unlawful crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-eight tax agents Liang Yong and Zhao Qin ran rampant; Zhengzhi arrested their henchman Li Ying and beat him to death, then laid out the two men's crimes at length.

sentences.zh: 欽亦以李英事訐奏，帝怒，命逮之。

translations.literal: Qin also denounced and memorialized on the Li Ying affair; the emperor was angry and ordered Zhengzhi seized.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qin also memorialized against Zhengzhi over the Li Ying affair; the emperor was furious and ordered his arrest.

sentences.zh: 給事中陳惟春言正誌劾欽罪多，宜提訊；

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Chen Weichun said Zhengzhi's impeachment of Qin listed many crimes and he ought to be summoned for interrogation;
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Chen Weichun said Zhengzhi had listed many crimes in impeaching Qin and should be summoned for interrogation;

sentences.zh: 欽所劾正誌事宜下撫按核實，免其逮系。

translations.literal: the matters Qin impeached against Zhengzhi ought to be sent down to the grand coordinator and regional inspector for verification, and his seizure and imprisonment waived.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's charges against Zhengzhi should be sent to the provincial authorities for verification, and Zhengzhi should not be arrested.

sentences.zh: 御史李時華亦言近日所逮吳應鴻、勞養魁、蔡如川、甘學書及正誌等，俱宜敕下撫按勘虛實，不得以一人單詞枉害良善。

translations.literal: Censor Li Shihua also said that those recently seized—Wu Yinghong, Lao Yangkui, Cai Ruchuan, Gan Xueshu, and Zhengzhi and others—ought all to be ordered sent down to the grand coordinator and regional inspector to investigate truth and falsehood, and that one person's single word must not wrongly harm the good.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Shihua also said that those recently arrested—Wu Yinghong, Lao Yangkui, Cai Ruchuan, Gan Xueshu, Zhengzhi, and others—should all be investigated by the provincial authorities, and that no honest man should be ruined on a single accuser's word.

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: None received reply.
translations.idiomatic: None of these pleas received a response.

sentences.zh: 未幾，梁永亦訐正誌。

translations.literal: Before long Liang Yong also denounced Zhengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liang Yong also denounced Zhengzhi.

sentences.zh: 帝命諸抗違欺隱者悉指名劾奏，重治之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that all who resisted, defied, or concealed be impeached by name and heavily punished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that all who resisted or concealed be impeached by name and punished severely.

sentences.zh: 宦官盆張，長吏皆喪氣。

translations.literal: Eunuchs flourished like a basin overflowing; senior officials all lost their spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs swarmed everywhere, and senior officials lost all courage.

sentences.zh: 正誌系詔獄四年，三十一年夏，瘐死。

translations.literal: Zhengzhi was imprisoned in the imperial prison four years; in the summer of the thirty-first year he died of illness in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengzhi spent four years in the imperial prison and died of illness there in the summer of year thirty-one.

sentences.zh: 天啟時，贈祭，蔭子，皆視鈺。

translations.literal: During Tianqi he was posthumously granted sacrifices and enrollment of a son, all as with Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi he received the same posthumous honors and enrollment of a son as Hua Yu.

sentences.zh: 自礦稅興，中使四出，跆藉有司。

translations.literal: Since mining taxes arose, inner envoys went out in all directions and trampled the regular officials.
translations.idiomatic: Once mining levies began, palace envoys went out in all directions and trampled the civil officials underfoot.

sentences.zh: 謗書一聞，駕帖立下。

translations.literal: At a single report of slander, the arrest warrant was issued at once.
translations.idiomatic: At the first whisper of slander, an arrest warrant was issued.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，則遼東參將梁心；

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year there was Liaodong battalion commander Liang Xin;
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-four it was Liaodong battalion commander Liang Xin;

sentences.zh: 二十五年，則山東福山知縣韋國賢；

translations.literal: in the twenty-fifth year, Shandong Fushan magistrate Wei Guoxian;
translations.idiomatic: in year twenty-five, Shandong Fushan magistrate Wei Guoxian;

sentences.zh: 二十六年，則山東益都知縣吳宗堯；

translations.literal: in the twenty-sixth year, Shandong Yidu magistrate Wu Zongyao;
translations.idiomatic: in year twenty-six, Shandong Yidu magistrate Wu Zongyao;

sentences.zh: 二十七年，則江西南康知府吳寶秀、星子知縣吳一元、山東臨清守備王煬；

translations.literal: in the twenty-seventh year, Jiangxi Nankang prefect Wu Baoxiu, Xingzi magistrate Wu Yiyuan, and Shandong Linqing garrison commander Wang Yang;
translations.idiomatic: in year twenty-seven, Jiangxi Nankang prefect Wu Baoxiu, Xingzi magistrate Wu Yiyuan, and Shandong Linqing garrison commander Wang Yang;

sentences.zh: 二十八年，則廣東新會在籍通判吳應鴻，舉人勞養魁、鐘聲朝、梁鬥輝，雲南尋甸知府蔡如川，趙州知州甘學書及正誌；

translations.literal: in the twenty-eighth year, Guangdong Xinhui enrolled vice prefect Wu Yinghong, provincial graduates Lao Yangkui, Zhong Shengchao, and Liang Douhui, Yunnan Xundian prefect Cai Ruchuan, Zhaozhou prefect Gan Xueshu, and Zhengzhi;
translations.idiomatic: in year twenty-eight, Guangdong Xinhui vice prefect Wu Yinghong, provincial graduates Lao Yangkui, Zhong Shengchao, and Liang Douhui, Yunnan Xundian prefect Cai Ruchuan, Zhaozhou prefect Gan Xueshu, and Zhengzhi;

sentences.zh: 二十九年，則湖廣按察僉事馮應京、襄陽通判邸宅、推官何棟如、棗陽知縣王之翰、武昌同知卞孔時、江西饒州通判陳奇可；

translations.literal: in the twenty-ninth year, Huguang surveillance vice commissioner Feng Yingjing, Xiangyang assistant prefect Di Zhai, investigating censor He Dongru, Zaoyang magistrate Wang Zhihan, Wuchang assistant prefect Bian Kongshi, and Jiangxi Raozhou vice prefect Chen Qike;
translations.idiomatic: in year twenty-nine, Huguang surveillance vice commissioner Feng Yingjing, Xiangyang assistant prefect Di Zhai, investigating censor He Dongru, Zaoyang magistrate Wang Zhihan, Wuchang assistant prefect Bian Kongshi, and Jiangxi Raozhou vice prefect Chen Qike;

sentences.zh: 三十年，則鳳陽臨淮知縣林錝；

translations.literal: in the thirtieth year, Fengyang Linhuai magistrate Lin Zheng;
translations.idiomatic: in year thirty, Fengyang Linhuai magistrate Lin Zheng;

sentences.zh: 三十四年，則陜西咸陽知縣宋時際；

translations.literal: in the thirty-fourth year, Shaanxi Xianyang magistrate Song Shiji;
translations.idiomatic: in year thirty-four, Shaanxi Xianyang magistrate Song Shiji;

sentences.zh: 三十五年，則陜西咸寧知縣滿朝薦；

translations.literal: in the thirty-fifth year, Shaanxi Xianning magistrate Man Chaojian;
translations.idiomatic: in year thirty-five, Shaanxi Xianning magistrate Man Chaojian;

sentences.zh: 三十六年，則遼東海防同知王邦才、參將李獲陽；

translations.literal: in the thirty-sixth year, Liaodong coastal-defense assistant prefect Wang Bangcai and battalion commander Li Huoyang;
translations.idiomatic: in year thirty-six, Liaodong coastal-defense assistant prefect Wang Bangcai and battalion commander Li Huoyang;

sentences.zh: 皆幽系詔獄，久者至十餘年。

translations.literal: all were secretly imprisoned in the imperial prison, the long-term cases reaching more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: all were thrown into the imperial prison, some for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 煬、應鴻、獲陽斃獄中，其他削籍、貶官有差。

translations.literal: Yang, Yinghong, and Huoyang died in prison; the others were struck from the rolls or demoted in office with varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yang, Wu Yinghong, and Li Huoyang died in prison; the others were struck from the rolls or demoted to varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 至士民幽系死亡者，尤不可勝紀也。

translations.literal: As for gentry and commoners secretly imprisoned who died, they especially cannot be fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry and common folk who were secretly imprisoned and died are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：神宗二十四年，軍府千戶仲春請開礦助大工，遂命戶部錦衣官各一人同仲春開采。

translations.literal: The commentator says: In the twenty-fourth year of Shenzong, the military-factory battalion commander Zhong Chun requested opening mines to aid great works; the court then ordered one official each from the Ministry of Revenue and the Embroidered-Uniform Guard to mine together with Zhong Chun.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: In the twenty-fourth year of Shenzong, military-factory battalion commander Zhong Chun proposed opening mines to fund great public works; the court then ordered one official each from the Ministry of Revenue and the Embroidered-Uniform Guard to mine with him.

sentences.zh: 給事中程紹言嘉靖中采礦，費帑金三萬餘，得礦銀二萬八千五百，得不償失，因罷其役。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Cheng Shao said that in the Jiajing reign mining had cost more than thirty thousand taels of treasury funds and yielded twenty-eight thousand five hundred taels of ore silver—the gain did not repay the loss—and therefore the undertaking was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Cheng Shao noted that under Jiajing, mining had cost more than thirty thousand taels of treasury funds while yielding only twenty-eight thousand five hundred taels of silver ore—a net loss—and the work was therefore halted.

sentences.zh: 給事中楊應文繼言之。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Yang Yingwen followed with the same argument.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Yang Yingwen repeated the argument.

sentences.zh: 皆不納。

translations.literal: None was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Neither memorial was heeded.

sentences.zh: 由是卑秩冗僚，下至市井黠桀，奮起言利。

translations.literal: From this, low-rank redundant officials down to market-place sharp scoundrels rose up to speak of profit.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, low-ranking officials and market schemers alike rushed forward with profit schemes.

sentences.zh: 而珰使四出，毒流海內，民不聊生，至三十三年乃罷。

translations.literal: Eunuch envoys went out in all directions, poison flowed through the realm, the people could not sustain life, and only in the thirty-third year was it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch agents spread everywhere, poison flowed across the realm, and the people could barely survive—only in year thirty-three was the policy halted.

sentences.zh: 嗣是軍興征發，加派再三。

translations.literal: Thereafter military campaigns arose and levies were dispatched; additional apportionments came again and again.
translations.idiomatic: After that came military campaigns, repeated levies, and surcharge upon surcharge.

sentences.zh: 府庫未充，膏脂已竭，明室之亡，於是決矣。

translations.literal: The government treasuries were not filled, yet the people's fat was already exhausted—the Ming house's fall was thereby decided.
translations.idiomatic: The treasuries were never filled, yet the people's substance was utterly drained—the fall of the Ming was thereby sealed.
